memory_update.text: ECVT should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for sulphuric-acid chokepoint work because it is a U.S.-listed small-cap with direct sulfuric acid recycling/regeneration and virgin acid production exposure.

HWKN is a weaker but useful discovery-lane hypothesis: it handles sulfuric acid as part of Industrial Solutions bulk chemical distribution, but acid-specific revenue, margin and allocation exposure must be verified before promotion.
MOS and FCX are reference anchors rather than underfollowed alpha candidates: they demonstrate downstream dependence on sulfur/sulfuric acid in phosphate fertilizers and copper SX-EW/leaching.

Need a separate pass for logistics/storage/tank-car/tanker names such as regulated liquid-bulk transport and acid storage assets; this Layer 1B pass found distributor exposure but did not fully map physical acid logistics.

node: Sulphur and sulphuric-acid feedstock for copper SX-EW, nickel HPAL and fertilizers
summary: Layer 1B expansion found two reference anchors and two underfollowed U.S.-listed discovery candidates. Reference anchors are large direct customers or integrated users of sulphur/sulphuric acid: Mosaic in phosphate fertilizers and Freeport-McMoRan in copper leaching/SX-EW. Underfollowed candidates are closer to the acid supply/distribution layer: Ecovyst as a North American sulphuric-acid recycler/virgin acid producer, and Hawkins as a specialty chemical distributor that explicitly stores and distributes sulphuric acid. The strongest node exposure among small/mid-cap names is ECVT; HWKN is a distribution/logistics hypothesis that needs product-level margin and regional tightness verification.
